To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) N- or B- tropic MuLVs can be mixed in the same virus particle; (2) such mixed particles are infectious for cells that do not exhibit FV-1 restriction, but are restricted when they infect either N- or F-type cells; (3) individual virus clones derived form such mixed particles have either N- or tropism, but not both; and (4) N- and B- tropic MSVs can be mixed in a virus particle
(1) MuLV particles can incorporate two types of envelope proteins into a single virion, and (2) the presence of a given envelope protein in a virion determines the tropism of that particle.

the tropism for N- or B-type cells is a phenotypically determined property of MuLV particles, that N- and b-type tropism is specified by different determinants, that the determinants are present in the virion, and that the presence of a given determinants renders a virion sensitive to Fv1 restriction in cells of opposite type.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of the Fv-1 system of genetic restriction of MuLV.
the molecular mechanisms of viral tropism.
the mechanisms by which the Fv-1 locus restricts the replication of MuLVs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the N and B tropism is not determined by the viral genome itself, but by the incorporation of different determinants into the virion, which in turn are determined by the type of the cell in which the virus is produced.
the N and B tropisms of murine leukemia viruses are determined by two different genetic determinants, which can be incorporated into virions and which are recognized by Fv-1.
phenotypic mixing between the N and the B-tropic viruses occurs in vivo, but not in vitro.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the tropism of the virus is determined by the presence of a particular determinant, and the sensitivity of the virus to Fv- 1 restriction is determined by the absence of a particular determinant.
N- and b-tropic MuLV particles contain two determinants that are recognized by the host Fv-1 gene.
the N and B tropism of MuLV is a phenotypically determined property.
The main takeaway from our work is that
phenotypic mixing between different viruses is a common and important phenomenon in virology.
the N- and B- tropic viruses are able to mix their phenotypes in the progeny virus particles.
the N and B tropism of MuLV is not determined by the viral envelope proteins, but instead is a property of the virion.
